newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia sorghum steady amid harvest-Grainco.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia sorghum steady amid harvest-Grainco.

text.p: Domestic Australian sorghum values were likely to remain steady with a lack of grower selling in the short to medium-term, Rob Brealey, trading manager of Queensland grain co-operative Grainco Ltd, said.
Lack of grower selling again characterised the domestic market while the export market continued to receive support from stronger corn markets, he said in Grainco's weekly market report.
Southern Queensland is in the middle of its sorghum harvest but only limited tonnage was traded in the past week, he said.
Values remained steady with both domestic consumers and the trade appearing to have sufficient coverage for the time being. Domestic prices finished the week on about A$142 a tonne.
Barley trade was light over the past week with prices remaining about the A$130 a tonne mark.
Emphasis had switched to sorghum with the harvest, he said.
Domestic malting barley values were lower with Grainco's bid finishing the week at A$170 a tonne Brisbane.
The domestic cottonseed market remained relatively flat at about A$120 a tonne in southern Queensland.
Concern was being expressed on the possibility of a downgrade in Australia's lint quality. While unlikely to affect seed quality, unfavourable weather had reduced yield estimates, he said.
New cottonseed business would be generated as awareness increased that supplies might not be in surplus, he said.

Domestic oilseed values remained steady over the past week, with sunflowers at A$310 a tonne Brisbane for March-April 1997, new crop soybean prices unchanged at A$400 a tonne Brisbane and canola lower at A$342 a tonne Moree for March-May delivery.
